body:
Not sure if this matters but maybe change this to
```suggestion
    let r_formatted = format!("v{}",  r_version);
```

This most likely won't work on unix-likes because the binary is usually installed under the name `R`.

```
bash-5.0$ r --version
bash: r: command not found
```
That is true, let me change this to an upper-case `R`.
Should this comment be about R not Node.js?

That seems a bit counter intuitive as usually, the variables get into the right side and static string on the left side. At least from the programming languages I have experience with but it seems the Rust documentation's examples show the same practices.

Maybe that project takes a different approach though? I can change it if that's the case, I don't mind.

My suggestion was simply to rather than have the format string, a static string and the variable just have a format string and the variable. Since the static string is not going to change we can simplify this to make it a bit easier to read but if it's not idiomatic rust maybe best to leave it the way it is.
Agree with andytom. Though this may not have effect on performance, it improves readability.

Hmm I must have been tired (or drunk 🍺 ) when I read the initial suggestion. Sorry @andytom , what you suggested is the idiomatic way. Even the Rust documentation I looked at indicates that (and I didn't leave the link as well... 🤷‍♂️ ). I probably mistaken the before and after. Changing this right now.
Works with me. Would be nice to have the R custom logo in there too.
